# A passive resistor-network realization of the intervention-order obstruction

**Root-origin construction; complementary analytic challenge and exact nodal checks.**
1 November 2026. This note binds the abstract signed-path obstruction to ordinary positive-conductance resistor networks. The response representation and earlier dark-path idea are inherited from Astra at revision `51ce47ce39f976517d60e2f87bbe280b651f6056`; this literal circuit realization and its analysis were developed in the present investigation. It is a theorem about a declared circuit class, not a claim that a laboratory circuit was built or calibrated.

## 1. Physical source, controls and receiver

Fix an integer n>=2, kappa>0 and delta>0. There are two boundary rails held at normalized potentials 0 and 1, and n+1 internal nodes numbered 0,...,n. Put s=2/kappa. At internal node j, install conductance s*a_j to rail 1 and conductance s*(1-a_j) to rail 0. A zero conductance means that branch is absent. All present conductances are positive.

The two sources have baseline internal potential vectors

    a_A=(0,1/2,...,1/2,0),
    a_B=(0,1/2,...,1/2,1).

Thus only the last internal node's anchor changes rails. Both retain total anchor conductance s at every internal node. Actuator i adds conductance u_i>=0 between internal nodes i-1 and i, for i=1,...,n. The dose budget is sum u_i<=delta. The receiver measures the total terminal current drawn from rail 1 at fixed unit voltage, equivalently effective conductance. It has no internal node probes and is not given the hidden anchor wiring. Actuator labels and allowable conductances are the same in both sources.

The lower bound is about the support of the complete actual added-conductance vector. A fully active reference network with one altered edge is a dense intervention. Off-state leakage would also have to be included in that complete command; the exact zero-support statement is a condition of this ideal circuit class, not an assertion about a particular switch.

## 2. Baseline and literal nodal equations

Let E be the n by n+1 incidence matrix with row i equal to e_i-e_(i-1), and U=diag(u). Kirchhoff's equations for internal potentials x are

    (s I + E^T U E)x = s a.                         (1)

The coefficient matrix is positive definite for every legal command. The actual rail-1 current is

    J(u)=sum_(j=0)^n s a_j(1-x_j).

# Simultaneous-intervention lower bound and conventional comparison

1 November 2026. Complementary derivation for the root investigation. All prior Astra source claims below refer only to revision `51ce47ce39f976517d60e2f87bbe280b651f6056` of `harjassand/astra-research-knowledge`.

## 1. Contract and notation

We observe scalar values of

    F(u)=g^T P(I+PBP)^(-1)Pg,
    P=diag(sqrt(u)), B>=0,
    |g_i|<=G, B_ii<=kappa,
    u>=0, sum_i u_i<=delta.

Assume delta,kappa,G>0 and write q=delta*kappa and L=delta*G^2. Here L is a global scale, not the actual input energy at a selected command. The experiment order is the support size of the complete actual command. A dense background plus one changed knob counts as dense.

The source representation and accepted determinant theorem are inherited from N1152. Its governing note is `research/2026-10-29-control-acquisition-and-matrix-formulas/source/p1-dark/selection/inference_determinant_tail_theorem.md`. The earlier path construction is `research/2026-10-29-control-acquisition-and-matrix-formulas/source/imports/DARK_INTERVENTION_ORDER.md` (Sections 2--4). That source was retrieved and read in full; its exact text is preserved alongside this note.

## 2. Main lower bound using the inherited path construction

For each integer n>=2 choose g=G(e_1+e_n), B_+=kappa*I+(kappa/4)*A_path, and flip the last offdiagonal edge sign to obtain B_-. Both are strictly positive definite with lower bound kappa/2. All proper-support responses agree at every nonnegative amplitude: the induced forest has at most one bright endpoint in each component, so a diagonal sign gauge can match B_+ to B_- while fixing g.

At u=(delta/n)1, let t=delta/n and a=kappa/4. Their shared determinant D_n obeys

    D_0=1, D_1=1+kappa*t,
    D_j=(1+kappa*t)D_(j-1)-(a*t)^2 D_(j-2).

The inherited cofactor identity gives the exact gap

    Delta_n=4 G^2 a^(n-1) t^n / D_n.

Because tr(t B)=q and B>=0, D_n<=exp(q). Therefore

    Delta_n >= (4L/n) exp(-q) [q/(4n)]^(n-1).       (P)

This quantified-in-n corollary is the useful addition here. The path construction and exact determinant/cofactor gap themselves are already Astra ingredients, and should not be claimed as newly invented.

# Simultaneous intervention order and the precision of a retained response law

28 October 2026. This extends the dark-channel example to every finite
intervention order and gives a complementary finite-accuracy boundary.
The source class and total physical dose language are exactly those of
`UNNORMALIZED_REPRESENTATION.md`.

## 1. Representation and actual experiment order

For c0>0, g in R^n and B positive semidefinite, the response is

    J(u)=c0+g^T P(I+PBP)^(-1)Pg,
    P=diag(sqrt(u)), u>=0, sum_i u_i<=delta.

The native scalar reaction is `R(u)=r0+J(u)` for a calibrated known r0.
Thus two J values differ by exactly the same amount as their raw R values.

An experiment has order at most k when the **complete actual command** u
has at most k nonzero coordinates. A dense shifted reference counts as part
of that command. Adding one new control on top of a dense active reference
is not an order-one experiment in this definition. Source resets, full
settings, actuation, settling, readout and return precision remain charged.

## 2. Every finite order misses some joint intervention

Fix k>=1, let m=k+1, and take n=m. Choose d>2a>0 and c0=1. Set

    g=e1+em,
    B_plus=dI+a A_path,

where A_path is the adjacency matrix of the path 1--2--...--m. B_minus
is identical except that the final off-diagonal pair (m-1,m),(m,m-1)
has value -a instead of +a. Both matrices are strictly positive definite:
Gershgorin gives a uniform lower eigenvalue bound d-2a>0. Their diagonals
are identically d. They are legal Schur families, with the canonical positive
source realization supplied by the unnormalized theorem.

**All lower-order responses agree.** For every proper support S subset of
{1,...,m}, and for every nonnegative command supported on S,

    J_plus(u)=J_minus(u).                              (1)

To prove this, restrict to S: zero command coordinates have no influence in
the P representation. The induced path is a forest of disjoint path segments.
Since S is proper, no component contains both bright endpoints 1 and m.
Two signings of a tree are related by a diagonal sign gauge. The free global
sign on each component can be chosen to fix its unique bright endpoint, if
it has one. Therefore a diagonal sign matrix D_S satisfies

    B_minus[S,S]=D_S B_plus[S,S] D_S,
    D_S g[S]=g[S].
